sheet-1.description: Sheet 1 of the June 1910 Sanborn atlas of Helmetta, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It carries the atlas title cartouche, the key, notes on water facilities and the fire department, and a long text block describing the American Snuff Co. works (Railroad Mills Snuff). Most of the sheet is the snuff mill complex between the head race and brook on the west and the railroad on the east: a long row of brick buildings for stamping, packing, curing, cutting and grinding tobacco, a storehouse for snuff flour, packing-box and wood-working shops, a lumber storehouse, empty-package and leaf-tobacco storehouses, a freight depot with platforms, water tanks, a stand pipe, gas tanks and a pump house. Maple runs across the upper part of the works and a drive runs past the snuff flour storehouse; a mill pond, the head race and the brook cross the lower half, with a wooden bridge. John runs north from Brookside Pl. along the leaf tobacco storehouses at the bottom of the sheet. On the east the R.R. (Amboy Div.) and Railroad Av. run beside Main St., with a few dwellings, a carpenter shop and iron storage on the east side of Main. Beyond a heavy line marking the P.R.R. a second road lettered Main passes a public school and scattered dwellings, and an Episcopal church stands at the lower right. Brookside Pl. along the bottom edge is drawn again at the top of sheet 2, which continues the town to the south.
notes: Modern John Street continues north from Brookside Place through the site of the 1910 snuff works to Maple Street; in 1910 John ended at the head race.
Maple is drawn on the line of modern Maple Street west of the mill; between the mill buildings and Main no street is drawn where Maple Street now meets Main Street.
The sheet is turned about 9 degrees further than sheet 2 so that the curving railroad runs straight up the page.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, north toward the upper left but turned about 9 degrees further than sheet 2 (north_deg -57.5 against -48.7), so that the curving Amboy branch runs straight up both sheets. Title, key and the American Snuff Co mill (Railroad Mills Snuff) with Main St, Railroad Av, Brookside Pl, John, Maple, the head race and brook; P.R.R. line and a second road lettered Main on the east. One part. Only Brookside Pl / John and Brookside Pl / Railroad Av detect (280 ft apart, on one line): placed from Brookside Pl / John with the scale of sheet 2 and north_deg -57.5, chosen so the modern Amboy Secondary track, Main Street and Maple Street lie on the drawn ones along the whole sheet (the two detected junctions alone give -60.8, but the same street is drawn 3 degrees off its modern bearing on sheet 2). Low confidence.

sheet-2-1.description: Main part of sheet 2 of the June 1910 Sanborn atlas of Helmetta, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left, continuing sheet 1 to the south. It covers the residential blocks south of Brookside Pl.: John runs down the west side of the sheet and Railroad Av. beside the R.R. (Amboy Div.) tracks on the east, crossed midway by Willow, and the street along the bottom of the sheet is lettered John again (today John Place). The blocks are lined with small one- and two-storey frame dwellings on narrow lots with sheds and outbuildings; the Avon Inn boarding house stands near Brookside Pl., and a passenger station sits beside the tracks. West of John a row of lots backs onto the brook, which runs down the left edge of the sheet; at the upper left two large American Snuff Co. storehouses for leaf tobacco are drawn behind John. East of the railroad Main runs past dwellings and a few outbuildings, with an open lot (block 5) and the brook curving through the upper right. Dashed water pipes are drawn in the streets, with hydrants at the corners. A heavy line at the lower right separates this part from an inset of tenements on John east of a brook (part 2), and a compass rose stands between them. The block numbers 2, 4 and 5 continue those of sheet 1.
notes: The John lettered along the bottom of the sheet is today John Place (OpenStreetMap), from John Street to Railroad Avenue.
Modern Willow Street continues east across the railroad to Main Street and Washington Avenue runs west from John Street; neither is drawn in 1910.
Brookside Place / Main Street was not detected: Main has only its east edge drawn beside the tracks.

Map, 50 ft to an inch, same orientation as sheet 1. Part 1: Brookside Pl south to John (now John Place) between the brook, John St, Railroad Av and Main St, with Willow. Part 2: inset at lower right behind a heavy line, John (house numbers 103-110, tenements) east of a brook, block 6; no cross street. Modern Willow Street east of Railroad Av to Main Street and Washington Avenue west of John Street are not drawn.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: tenements and dwellings on John east of a brook, block 6 (no street junction (one street only, location east of the brook not identified with a modern street); needs identification of the street on the ground, then parcel corners (locate.py corner) or carried points).
